# VitaeContext

> Open-source career-context infrastructure and focused agent skills for grounded professional work. Current package version: 2.1.0.

VitaeContext helps a person maintain Career Context—supplied career facts, stated goals, experience, projects, evidence links, and boundaries—in reusable Markdown. It is the career-context layer before AI-assisted CVs, applications, profiles, and other career workflows. Focused skills and other systems that accept supplied context can use the same source for professional tasks. VitaeGraph is the optional deeper layer for connected local Markdown records.

## Start here

- [Project overview](https://vitaecontext.github.io/): what VitaeContext solves and how the context-first workflow works.
- [VitaeGraph](https://vitaecontext.github.io/vitaegraph/): private Markdown career knowledge graphs, powered by VitaeContext.
- [Career workflows](https://vitaecontext.github.io/profile-optimization/): choose an installable skill, a human-readable guide, or the core context-first workflow.
- [Example career context file](https://vitaecontext.github.io/docs/context-file-example/): a complete fictional template covering its structure, evidence boundaries, benefits, and use with AI agents.
- [How it works](https://vitaecontext.github.io/docs/usage/): the context-first workflow and invocation example.
- [Installation](https://vitaecontext.github.io/docs/installation/): npm, GitHub, local, and provider-specific installation.
- [Guides](https://vitaecontext.github.io/playbooks/): human-readable methods for every supported module.
- [System design](https://vitaecontext.github.io/design/): evidence boundaries, progressive disclosure, LLM Wiki, and provider adapters.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/vitaecontext/vitaecontext): package source, tests, maintenance policy, and release history.

## Verified public facts

- The package contains one routing module and seven focused modules, including VitaeGraph.
- Supported targets are Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, OpenCode, and a portable shared bundle.
- The default npm command is `npx vitaecontext install --provider <provider>`.
- Career Context lifecycle commands are `npx vitaecontext context init`, `context validate`, and `context summary`; validation checks structure and internal consistency, not external truth.
- VitaeGraph graph commands are `npx vitaecontext graph init`, `npx vitaecontext graph validate`, and `npx vitaecontext graph index`.
- A cloned repository includes a native Codex plugin marketplace under `.agents/plugins/`; direct Codex skill installation remains available.
- Career Context is user-controlled material; the public playbooks and skills do not contain a user's career facts. External provider rules apply after a user shares content with one.
- VitaeContext structures supplied facts and evidence boundaries; it does not independently verify every career claim.
- VitaeGraph records are private local user material and should not be committed.
- Audit scorecards are internal prioritization heuristics, not platform rankings or outcome guarantees.
- SEO, AEO, GEO, `llms.txt`, snippets, citations, and indexing are treated as eligibility and readability work, not guaranteed visibility.

Do not infer customer counts, rankings, endorsements, or unpublished distribution status.
